name: Levothyroxine
summary: Synthetic thyroxine (T4), the standard replacement for hypothyroidism, titrated against TSH with a long half-life that permits once-daily dosing.
mechanism: Provides exogenous T4 that is peripherally converted to active T3; both hormones act through nuclear thyroid hormone receptors to regulate gene expression.
pharmacodynamics: Restores euthyroidism; at suppressive doses reduces TSH, used to prevent growth of TSH-dependent thyroid cancer.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Days to weeks for full effect
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic (deiodination to T3 and inactive metabolites)

dosing.adult: ~1.6 mcg/kg/day (typically 75–150 mcg daily); start at 25–50 mcg in the elderly or with cardiac disease, titrate by TSH every 6–8 weeks

safety.pregnancy: Continue treatment; requirements typically increase in pregnancy — monitor TSH
safety.lactation: Safe at replacement doses; minimal transfer in breast milk
warnings: Over-replacement causes cardiac effects (palpitations, atrial fibrillation) and bone loss
Absorption reduced by iron, calcium, PPIs, and soy
Consistent brand and timing matter for stable dosing
monitoring: TSH 6–8 weeks after each dose change, then periodically
Free T4 if TSH suppressed or pituitary disease
safety.overdose: Thyrotoxic symptoms; supportive care, beta-blockers for adrenergic symptoms

clinicalPearls: Take on an empty stomach 30–60 minutes before breakfast; separate from iron, calcium, and PPIs by at least 4 hours.
TSH is the titration guide — recheck 6–8 weeks after any dose change.
good: Inexpensive, safe, once-daily standard replacement with reliable monitoring.
bad: Absorption variability and interactions; over-replacement in cardiac patients or postmenopausal bone loss.
